measures.designation: Constitutional Amendment - Increasing Funding to School Districts
measures.subject: Permanent school fund distributions to school districts
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Minnesota Constitution be amended to increase the funding going to all school districts from the permanent school fund, which is a fund that supports school districts without raising individual income or property taxes, effective July 1, 2027?
measures.summary: Would change the constitutional rules for managing the permanent school fund so it preserves purchasing power over time and distributes money to school districts under a policy set by law, with a companion statute setting annual distributions at 4.5% of the fund's three-year average value starting July 1, 2027.

measureEffectiveNote: The ballot question itself states the change is 'effective July 1, 2027', and Laws 2026, ch. 114, sec. 6 makes the companion statutory distribution changes effective July 1, 2027 (aid payable in fiscal year 2028) if voters adopt the amendment. Adoption requires a majority of all voters casting ballots at the election (Minn. Const. art. IX, sec. 1); a blank answer counts as no.
notes: Candidate names and party codes come from the Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 election-results feed (electionresultsfiles.sos.mn.gov/20261103/*.txt), which is pre-loaded with the general-election ballot; its vote figures are pre-election test data and were ignored.

Party labels are as printed on a Hennepin County SD45/HD45A sample ballot (DFL = 'Democratic-Farmer-Labor', GP = 'Green', LIB = 'Libertarian', FI = 'Forward Independence', IND = 'Independent'); that ballot matched the SOS feed for every statewide race and CD3.

Major-party nominees match the official Aug 11, 2026 primary results (e.g. Flanagan over Craig; Tafoya over Schwarze and White; Klobuchar/Schierer; Demuth/Wilson over Lindell and Qualls; Nagel won the CD5 GOP primary).
U.S. Senate is the regular Class 2 seat (Tina Smith not running); no special election.

Minnesota judicial races are nonpartisan; every 2026 statewide judicial seat has only the incumbent printed. 'Nonpartisan' is used as the party value; the ballot prints 'Incumbent' instead of a party.

There is one statewide constitutional amendment (Laws 2026, ch. 114, HF 3900). The ballot heading is 'Constitutional Amendments' with the title 'Increasing Funding to School Districts'; it is not numbered. Ballot title in law is 'Increasing funding to school districts.'
All of Minnesota is in the Central time zone; polls close 8:00 PM CST (UTC-6) on Nov 3, 2026.
unconfirmed: CD5: DeVelle L. Jackson's printed party label. The SOS feed code is IND (same code printed as 'Independent' for Simonetti) and a sample-ballot blog post shows 'Independent', but The Ballot Brief reports 'Independence-Alliance Party'. 'Independent' used.
Party labels for CD1, CD2, CD4-CD8 were not seen on a printed ballot; inferred from the SOS party codes using the Hennepin sample ballot's spellings.

The official SOS candidate-filing site (candidates.sos.mn.gov) and sos.mn.gov ballot pages were blocked by a captcha, so no candidate withdrawals or changes after the feed was loaded could be checked against them directly.
